sanskrit_verse: स्वम् अप्यर्थं तथा नष्टं लब्ध्वा राज्ञे निवेदयेत् । गृह्णीयात् तत्र तं शुद्धम् अशुद्धं स्यात् ततोऽन्यथा ॥
transliteration: svam apy arthaṃ tathā naṣṭaṃ labdhvā rājñe nivedayet | gṛhṇīyāt tatra taṃ śuddham aśuddhaṃ syāt tato'nyathā ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who recovers their own property or another's lost property must report it to the sovereign authority. The sovereign shall receive it in its purified state; otherwise, it becomes impure by inversion of ownership.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides solely in the sovereign as representative of Dharma
Causation arises through rightful knowledge and declaration of ownership
Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of lawful possession
Restoration logic demands return of assets without contamination of intent
Consciousness alignment occurs when ownership reflects truth and integrity
executable_legal_axioms: IF an entity recovers a lost asset AND identifies original ownership THEN report to sovereign authority
IF sovereign receives asset without malafide intent THEN asset remains pure AND restorable
IF asset is retained without reporting THEN purity status degrades AND misalignment accrues
IF claimant presents valid pramāṇa THEN sovereign MUST restore asset without punitive inquiry
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, this verse establishes that recovery and restitution are acts of dharma requiring immediate reporting to the sovereign. The Court serves as the final interpreter of purity of title, ensuring no inversion of ownership occurs due to delay or negligence.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality ensures rightful ownership is established through evidence, not punishment. Anupūrvaśaḥ applies as sequential manifestation of ownership from loss to recovery to restoration. Responsibility aligns proportionally with knowledge and capacity. There is no punitive consequence—only correction of ownership integrity.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Asset must be reported within prescribed time to retain purity status
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Sovereign assumes custodial role upon notification
Capacity Restoration: Claimants must demonstrate pramāṇa for lawful retrieval
Integrity Reintegration: Ownership inversion is corrected through conscious reaffirmation
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands declared: Ownership is purified through conscious restoration, not punitive enforcement. Dharma prevails through alignment with truth. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the supreme adjudicator.
